title: fix(gateway): settle restart intents and update reports in workers
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Restart-intent consumption could block the Gateway signal thread behind a SQLite writer, then return an intent whose separate deletion failed. A later signal could consume it again. Update-report receipts also used main-thread SQLite and needed accepted work to settle before their transport and storage owners closed.

Runtime intent consumption, handoff writes, report receipt transitions, and cleanup now use their existing workers. Intent consumption is atomic `DELETE … RETURNING`; duplicate suppression, current publication authority, and accepted-work settlement remain intact.

The schema-cache parent #167001 merged and its branch was deleted, so this PR targets `main`. Approved-head lane proof below compares **`c786f4d4c4ea27630466a529630e56071845a682` → `b48f88f9f3f6eafedfce6b06bc227f38c3b209c6`**. Parent/cache improvements are inherited and are not credited to this change.

## Ownership and restart readiness

The shared-state writer owns runtime intent consumption and handoff persistence. The sentinel writer owns receipt reservation, transitions, finalization, and cleanup; its read worker supplies receipt reads. Callers capture physical database identity before yielding. Authoritative rereads and writes remain synchronous inside worker transactions, with live authority checked again at transaction, commit, and publication boundaries. Commit receipts reconcile lost replies without replaying accepted writes. Reservation-bound artifact paths prevent delayed cleanup from deleting a successor's report.

The signal owner preserves FIFO and joins accepted intent work before close. The report RPC uses its existing execution join so connection retirement waits for receipt and cleanup settlement. Supervisor handoff persistence remains **after canonical writer drain and the final restart decision**.

Real restart proof showed that cold worker code loading was on the readiness critical path. Restart operations now use the existing lightweight registry, and an accepted supervised restart may preload **code only** while shutdown proceeds. Preparation opens no database and performs no schema admission, intent consumption, or handoff write. It uses existing broker capacity and can be preempted by ordinary work. Post-drain admission still obtains fresh physical identity and current grants; it never reuses a retiring database handle. Unavailable preparation retains cold admission; genuine capacity preemption permits a fresh cold open. Failed, stale, foreign, or reused preparation handles reject. Cleanup remains owned and joined.

Six alternating base/candidate pairs on one Hetzner Linux host, Node **24.21.0**, passed real RPC restart, clean predecessor exit, successor identity, persisted handoff restoration, HTTP readiness, authenticated reconnect, first successful `sessions.list`, and process cleanup. All twelve runs passed. The first-accepted-request median increase is **193.778 ms**, within the specified **≤200 ms** gate.

| Request to… | Base ms, median [min–max] | Candidate ms, median [min–max] | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Old-process exit | 1217.636 [1198.114–1236.765] | 1335.880 [1310.858–1345.592] | +118.244 ms |
| HTTP ready | 10799.374 [10738.711–11005.353] | 11026.566 [10847.233–11132.587] | +227.192 ms |
| First accepted authenticated RPC | 11025.382 [10971.642–11221.799] | 11219.160 [11068.497–11373.654] | +193.778 ms |

This pass has **6.222 ms of median headroom**. HTTP readiness alone increased by **227.192 ms**; the specified gate is the first accepted authenticated request. The observed handoff log span was **32.647 [30.057–45.109] → 123.319 [113.119–128.458] ms**; that is a log-receipt diagnostic, not native-operation timing. These results cover normal capacity and an isolated external supervisor, not native macOS/Windows timing or a universal latency bound. Saturation can decline or preempt optional preparation and retain the correct cold fallback. Earlier candidates exceeded the readiness budget; the final result is the measured prewarming implementation.

Schema, durability, retention, permissions, configuration, and released synchronous SDK contracts are unchanged. Native boot/supervisor handoff consumption and service CLI lock primitives retain their documented synchronous contracts. An inherited unused internal `ClientVoiceToolEffect` type export was made private to satisfy Knip; it has no released SDK export path.

## Final direct statements and requests

Three strictly alternating pairs exercise the real report handler with synthetic GitHub transport and current system-operator authority, then receipt/restart operations through their compiled shared writer. Counts include every observed thread/helper and zero-SQL requests. All count ranges below are deterministic across the three runs; full ranges remain in the phase table.

| Flow | ALL statements | MAIN statements | Worker requests |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Created submit/finalize/cleanup | 154 → 149 | 56 → 20 | 25 → 31 |
| Reconcile/finalize/cleanup | 40 → 38 | 20 → 4 | 5 → 8 |
| Uncertain submission | 140 → 136 | 42 → 20 | 25 → 29 |
| Warm intent consumption | 30 → 6 | 30 → 0 | 0 → 1 |
| Post-drain handoff | 87 → 83 | 87 → 0 | 0 → 2 |
| Preparation + drain + handoff + release | 93 → 89 | 92 → 5 | 2 → 4 |
| Code preparation / preparation release | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 |
| Product operations | **652 → 612** | **368 → 64** | **70 → 106** |
| All phases, including setup and verification | **3369 → 3338** | **2830 → 2318** | **2055 → 2140** |

Worker placement is not an all-thread saving. This change reduces direct product statements by **40**, while adding **36 product worker requests**. The complete fixture reduces statements by **31** and adds **85 requests**, including source-loader/initialization, setup, lifecycle, and verification requests. Preparation costs are included; none are hidden in an uncounted warm-up.

Cold handoff removes one timeout read (2→1), two timeout assignments (6→4), and the WAL-autocheckpoint read/disable (1+1→0+0), while retaining one additional combined version observation (2→3): **−1−2−2+1=−4**. Numeric timeout values are grouped within each run before taking medians. Requests add exactly open + handoff. Preparation's approximately 2 ms host phase only starts code loading; imports may continue through the fully counted drain/handoff phases.

- **Created submit/finalize/cleanup −5:** five fewer ownership SELECTs (`inspectOpenClawStateOwnershipFromDatabase` / `assertOpenClawStateWriteAllowed`). Domain receipt transitions and their transaction envelopes remain. Added requests: receipt read, reserve, mark prepared, mark pending, finalize, complete cleanup.
- **Duplicate −2 and reconciliation −2:** one ownership SELECT and one schema-content-version SELECT removed from each. Duplicate adds one receipt-read request; reconciliation adds receipt read, finalize, and complete cleanup.
- **Each preview −1:** one ownership SELECT removed; requests unchanged.
- **Uncertain submission −4:** five ownership SELECTs removed, offset by one required content-version read. Added requests: receipt read, reserve, mark prepared, mark pending.
- **Receipt/sweep-lease reads +1 each; artifact sweep +1:** the current read-only worker retains one schema-content-version SELECT through `readStateSchemaContentVersionRow` → `readContentVersionMarker` → `assertSupportedStateSchemaVersion`. The actual receipt SELECT and foreign-commit observation remain. This is an explicit required-freshness cost, not unrelated noise. The current base reuses the previously separate schema/user-version observations; stale cleanup remains **7→7**.
- **Warm intent −24:** separate SELECT+DELETE becomes one `DELETE ... RETURNING` (−1 domain statement). Repeated native admission removes 24 statements—seven schema/user-version probes, six catalog reads, three table-existence reads, two integrity checks, two busy-timeout operations, and one each of direct data-version, schema metadata, ownership, and content-version reads—offset by one additional combined version observation. Net native admission −23; total −24. One `restartLifecycle.consumeIntent` request is added.
- **Cold handoff −4:** the normalized timeout/WAL/version decomposition above.

The complete product SQL delta is **−5−2−2−1−1−4−24−4+1+1+1 = −40**. Ordinary reservation stays **6→6**, ordinary receipt transitions stay **7→7**, and warm handoff stays **6→6**; each adds one worker request and moves MAIN work to its existing worker. File-only save/publish/discard stays zero SQL and zero requests. No unchanged operation is presented as an ALL-thread saving.

**Every added product request**

These counts sum to **+36** per measured product cycle in each pair. All requests, including zero-SQL requests, are retained.

| Family | Request | Added per product cycle |
|---|---|---:|
| sqlite-broker | `open` | +1 |
| sqlite-broker | `restartLifecycle.consumeIntent` | +1 |
| sqlite-broker | `restartLifecycle.writeHandoff` | +2 |
| sqlite-broker | `restartSentinel.beginCleanup` | +1 |
| sqlite-broker | `restartSentinel.beginStaleCleanup` | +1 |
| sqlite-broker | `restartSentinel.claimSweep` | +2 |
| sqlite-broker | `restartSentinel.completeCleanup` | +5 |
| sqlite-broker | `restartSentinel.finalizeReceipt` | +3 |
| sqlite-broker | `restartSentinel.markPending` | +3 |
| sqlite-broker | `restartSentinel.markPrepared` | +3 |
| sqlite-broker | `restartSentinel.refreshPreparation` | +1 |
| sqlite-broker | `restartSentinel.releaseSweep` | +2 |
| sqlite-broker | `restartSentinel.reserve` | +3 |
| task-worker | `restartSentinel.reportReceipt` | +8 |

**Complete-window accounting**

Initialization is **−50 SQL/+38 requests**: import SQL is unchanged, with one extra source-loader request; fixture warming is −50 SQL/+37 requests, including two source-loader requests and 35 domain requests. Warming exercises intent twice (−48 statements combined) and receipt paths (eight ownership reads removed, six content-version reads added, net −2). These initialization effects are separate from the product saving.

Fixture setup is **−2 SQL/+2 requests**: created and uncertain setup each remove one ownership SELECT; abort/stale setup reserves add their worker requests. Lifecycle is **+1 SQL/+1 request**, from one additional final `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` and its worker close; canonical drain and preparation release do not add SQL or requests.

Verification is **+60 SQL/+8 requests**: the same-process native boot verifier after worker-only handoff independently admits MAIN (**13→92, +79**); the second intent consume saves 24; receipt verification adds five content-version reads. **+79−24+5=+60**. Warm native boot verification is unchanged at13. The cold verifier is explicit fixture lifecycle work and is retained in all-phase totals; it is not a claim about a separately spawned successor process.

The complete conservation is **−50−2−40+1+60=−31 SQL**, and **+38+2+36+1+8=+85 requests**. Source-loader tooling accounts for three of those added initialization requests. Production/initialization/request differences are not silently discarded.

The inherited duplicate **+267 schema-construction statements remain absent**. On the current base, receipt/sweep-lease reads are **2 → 3**, stale cleanup **7 → 7**, and artifact sweep **18 → 19**. Required freshness checks remain; subsequent base admission/cache improvements explain the difference from the previously accepted 2→5, 7→9, and 18→21 observations. Final direct runs have **zero failed native executions**, including intent consumption and exactly-once verification.

## Accepted shared chat and shutdown evidence

The coordinator accepted six alternating pairs at historical base **`b881e1423c4a10bfc338f823dccefadcf996261d`** and candidate **`a1cd0d8e3cc3ca8756be17250c028cac08a5837e`**. These are retained as historical W6 evidence, **not measurements of the final head against current main**. A final source audit confirms preparation requires an accepted supervised restart, so it is inactive in first/warmed chat and the fixture's SIGTERM stop. Ordinary broker SQL/request envelopes and the atomic intent kernel remain unchanged by preparation. Independent base freshness/admission changes prevent transplanting historical absolute totals onto the final base.

Warmed turns were **1513.45 → 1513.1 ALL**, **6.5 → 6.5 MAIN**, and **299 → 299.1 requests/turn**. No chat-turn saving, global request reduction, or under-500-turn claim is made. Total shared requests were **4744.5 → 4754.5**.

Raw first-turn statements were **3482 → 3505 (+23)**. The accepted deferred-startup window was **boot+connect+first 6225.5 → 6222**; conservatively retaining every other origin leaves **3448 → 3434.5** first-turn statements. Only post-ready plugin maintenance, pairing notification, outbound recovery, remote catalog refresh, and cron startup planning were classified as deferred startup. First/warmed traces had zero intersections with W6 files changed at that measured head. Connect uses boot+connect **2741 → 2763.5 (+0.8209%)**. Second-session +0.3735% and cron +0.2073% belong to unchanged owners and fit the non-turn allowance. Every shared phase has a duration ratio ≤1.5.

Historical shutdown was **702 → 679.5 ALL**, **202 → 150 MAIN**, and **82 → 75 requests**. The W6 saving is intent consumption **41 → 6 ALL**, **41 → 0 MAIN**, with **one added worker request**: SELECT+DELETE→DELETE RETURNING removes one domain statement; repeated native admission removes 34 others (11 schema/user-version probes, 11 catalog reads, three table-existence reads, two busy-timeout operations, two integrity checks, and one each of schema metadata, quarantine, ownership, content-version, and comparison-table work).

The median-supplying shutdown observations decompose as intent **−37** plus unchanged owners **+14.5** = **−22.5**; intent's standalone median is −35 because different observations supply those medians. Memory admission is the largest positive background component, offset by native closure/WAL, placement, session, and memory settlement. Thread movement and unrelated background decreases are not credited as W6 savings.

Historical shared traces had **zero intent lock refusals**. Their 13 other refusals belong to unchanged owners: 11 startup plugin-lease releases and two audit-prune refusals, one per side. Final direct runs had zero failed native executions; final readiness and driver logs had zero observed lock-refusal diagnostics. Readiness was uninstrumented and does not replace the historical all-thread refusal count. This is not a globally lock-free-shutdown claim.
